# IC Reactor Full LLM Guide

Use this file when an AI assistant needs enough context to write or review IC
Reactor code without reading the whole repository. Use `llms.txt` first for a
compact manifest and package routing table.

## What IC Reactor Is

IC Reactor v3 is a TypeScript/React monorepo for Internet Computer apps. It wraps
typed canister calls with TanStack Query caching, reusable query/mutation
objects, React hooks, optional Internet Identity auth helpers, runtime Candid
parsing, and code generation from `.did` files.

This documentation targets the stable `@ic-reactor/core` v3.12.0 runtime release.

## Package Boundaries

| Package                   | Responsibility                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@ic-reactor/core`        | Framework-agnostic runtime with `ClientManager`, `Reactor`, `DisplayReactor`, and `@tanstack/query-core` integration. No React imports. |
| `@ic-reactor/react`       | React hooks, `createActorHooks`, query/mutation factories, Internet Identity auth, and identity-attribute hooks.                         |
| `@ic-reactor/candid`      | Runtime Candid fetching/parsing adapters, `CandidReactor`, display variants, and metadata reactors.                                     |
| `@ic-reactor/parser`      | Rust/WASM Candid parser. One entrypoint (`@ic-reactor/parser`); conditional exports pick the browser or Node build.                     |
| `@ic-reactor/codegen`     | Shared generator pipeline for declarations, reactor files, stable wrappers, and client helpers.                                         |
| `@ic-reactor/cli`         | CLI around `@ic-reactor/codegen`, config loading, commands, and schema.                                                                 |
| `@ic-reactor/vite-plugin` | Vite watch-mode generation and local IC environment injection.                                                                          |

## Install

React apps:

```bash
pnpm add @ic-reactor/react @icp-sdk/core @tanstack/react-query
```

Non-React apps:

```bash
pnpm add @ic-reactor/core @icp-sdk/core @tanstack/query-core
```

Auth helpers:

```bash
pnpm add @ic-reactor/react @icp-sdk/auth
```

The `@icp-sdk/auth` peer is `^8`; v7 is no longer supported. pnpm and yarn
install this set as published. A strict `npm install` fails with `ERESOLVE`,
because every published `@icp-sdk/auth` still peers `@icp-sdk/core@^5` while
`@ic-reactor/react` needs `^6` — stale metadata rather than an actual
incompatibility. For npm, add to `package.json`:

```json
{ "overrides": { "@icp-sdk/auth": { "@icp-sdk/core": "$@icp-sdk/core" } } }
```

Dynamic Candid:

```bash
pnpm add @ic-reactor/candid @ic-reactor/parser
```

## One-Call Setup

`defineReactor` creates the `QueryClient`, `ClientManager`, reactor, and bound
hooks in one call. `display: true` selects `DisplayReactor` instead of `Reactor`.

```ts
import { defineReactor } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { idlFactory, type _SERVICE } from "./declarations/backend"

export const backendApp = defineReactor<_SERVICE>({
  name: "backend",
  idlFactory,
  display: true,
})

export const {
  reactor: backend,
  queryClient,
  useActorQuery,
  useActorMutation,
  useActorMethod,
  useAuth,
  useIdentityAttributes,
} = backendApp
```

It returns the six `createActorHooks` hooks plus `useAuth`, `useAgentState`,
`useUserPrincipal`, `useIdentityAttributes`, and the underlying `reactor`,
`clientManager`, `queryClient`, `authentication`, and `identityAttributes`.
`authentication` and `identityAttributes` are lazy getters, so the optional
`@icp-sdk/auth` peer is only loaded once auth is actually touched. Omitting the
peer builds everywhere; webpack-family bundlers print one `Module not found`
warning for it because the import is declared optional, silenceable with
`ignoreWarnings: [{ module: /@ic-reactor\/react/, message: /@icp-sdk\/auth/ }]`.

To share one agent and one Internet Identity session across canisters, pass the
first result's `authentication` into the next call:

```ts
import { idlFactory as indexIdl, type _SERVICE as _INDEX } from "./declarations/index_canister"

export const indexApp = defineReactor<_INDEX>({
  name: "index",
  idlFactory: indexIdl,
  authentication: backendApp.authentication,
})
```

Passing `authentication` alone is enough — its `clientManager` is adopted.
Passing a *different* `clientManager` alongside it throws, because sign-in would
update one agent while the reactor calls through another.

## Manual Runtime Setup

Use this when construction order or dependency injection needs to be explicit.

```ts
import { ClientManager, DisplayReactor } from "@ic-reactor/core"
import { createActorHooks } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { QueryClient } from "@tanstack/query-core"
import { idlFactory, type _SERVICE } from "./declarations/backend"

export const queryClient = new QueryClient()
export const clientManager = new ClientManager({ queryClient })

export const backend = new DisplayReactor<_SERVICE>({
  clientManager,
  idlFactory,
  name: "backend",
})

export const { useActorQuery, useActorMutation } = createActorHooks(backend)
```

Use `DisplayReactor` for UI/form code. Use `Reactor` when raw Candid values are
required.

## Pattern Selection

| Need                              | Preferred API                                  | Works outside React                                                |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Component hooks with one canister | `defineReactor(params)`                        | No                                                                 |
| Explicit construction order       | `ClientManager` + `Reactor` + `createActorHooks` | No                                                               |
| Generic component hooks           | `createActorHooks(reactor)`                    | No                                                                 |
| Method-specific reusable reads    | `createQuery`, `createSuspenseQuery`           | Yes: `.fetch()`, `.prefetch()`, `.invalidate()`, `.getCacheData()` |
| Paginated reads                   | `createInfiniteQuery`, suspense variant        | Yes: `.fetch()`, `.invalidate()`, `.getCacheData()`                |
| Reusable updates                  | `createMutation`                               | Yes: `.execute(args)`                                              |
| One imperative component call API | `useActorMethod`                               | No                                                                 |
| Larger `.did`-driven apps         | `@ic-reactor/vite-plugin` or `@ic-reactor/cli` | No — generated exports are hooks; use the generated reactor's `.fetchQuery()` / `.callMethod()` |

## Inside React vs Outside React

Only call React hooks inside React components or custom hooks:

- `useActorQuery`
- `useActorMutation`
- `useActorMethod`
- `.useQuery()`
- `.useMutation()`
- `.useSuspenseQuery()`
- `.useInfiniteQuery()`

Outside React, use imperative methods:

- query `.fetch()`, `.prefetch()`, `.invalidate()`, `.getCacheData()`,
  `.setData()`
- mutation `.execute(args)`
- reactor `.fetchQuery()`, `.getQueryData()`, `.invalidateQueries()`,
  `.callMethod()`

## Reusable Factory Example

```ts
import { createMutation, createQueryFactory } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { backend } from "./reactor"

export const getProfile = createQueryFactory(backend, {
  functionName: "get_profile",
})

export const updateProfile = createMutation(backend, {
  functionName: "update_profile",
})
```

Inside React:

```tsx
const profileQuery = getProfile(["alice"])
const { data } = profileQuery.useQuery()
const { mutateAsync } = updateProfile.useMutation({
  invalidateQueries: [profileQuery.getQueryKey()],
})
```

Outside React:

```ts
const profileQuery = getProfile(["alice"])
await profileQuery.fetch()
const cached = profileQuery.getCacheData()
await updateProfile.execute([{ name: "Alice" }])
await profileQuery.invalidate()
```

Prefer `query.getQueryKey()` or `query.invalidate()` over hard-coded cache keys.

## Auth

`@ic-reactor/react` owns `AuthenticationManager`,
`IdentityAttributesManager`, auth constants/types, and React hooks over those
managers.

```ts
import {
  AuthenticationManager,
  IdentityAttributesManager,
  createAuthHooks,
  createIdentityAttributeHooks,
} from "@ic-reactor/react"

export const authentication = new AuthenticationManager({ clientManager })
export const { useAuth, useAgentState, useUserPrincipal } =
  createAuthHooks(authentication)

export const identityAttributes = new IdentityAttributesManager(authentication)
export const { useIdentityAttributes } =
  createIdentityAttributeHooks(identityAttributes)
```

`createAuthHooks` takes an `AuthenticationManager`, never a `ClientManager`, and
returns exactly `useAuth`, `useAgentState`, and `useUserPrincipal`.
`useIdentityAttributes` comes only from `createIdentityAttributeHooks`.

Pass identity-attribute nonces as a callback
(`nonce: () => backend.callMethod({ functionName: "register_begin" })`).
Awaiting the nonce before the call ends the user gesture and the browser blocks
the Internet Identity window.

### Local Internet Identity

`localInternetIdentityProvider(port, canisterId?, authorizePath?)` builds
`http://<canisterId>.localhost:<port>/authorize`. Which path works depends on the
installed II build, so `AuthenticationManager.prepareClient()` probes the
canister over the agent and selects `/authorize` or the legacy `/#authorize`, and
rejects login outright when the build serves neither.

Only builds up to `release-2026-03-16` work locally: `release-2025-03-07` and
earlier serve the SPA at `/` with a `#authorize` fragment, `release-2026-01-05`
through `release-2026-03-16` serve `/authorize`, and from `release-2026-03-23` the
frontend left the canister entirely (the id.ai split). A local login that hangs on
the gateway's "Response Verification Error" page is an unsupported II build —
install `internet_identity_dev.wasm` from `release-2026-03-16`.

## Error Handling (Important)

IC Reactor distinguishes canister business errors from transport/runtime errors.

| Error kind | Typical source | Preferred handling |
| ---------- | -------------- | ------------------ |
| `CanisterError` | `Result.Err` returned by canister methods | `onCanisterError` (for hooks/factories), or `isCanisterError(...)` in try/catch |
| `CallError` | network/agent issues (timeouts, unreachable canister, etc.) | `onError` or `isCallError(...)` |
| `ValidationError` | `DisplayReactor` argument validators | `isValidationError(...)` and show field errors |

`CanisterError` carries the raw canister error value on `.err` — not `.detail`,
`.data`, or `.message`. `.code` is the variant key, or the `code` field when the
payload follows the ApiError shape, and `.details` is the optional `Map`. Always
read the payload from `.err`.

When using mutations, prefer:

- `onCanisterError` for logic errors from canister `Err` variants
- `onError` for broad fallback handling across all error types

Do not use only `onError` when business logic needs distinct UX messaging.

## Code Generation

Use generated hooks when canisters are large, `.did` files change often, or
consistent typed exports matter.

| Tool                      | Use when                                                                      |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@ic-reactor/vite-plugin` | Vite app, watch-mode regeneration, local environment injection                |
| `@ic-reactor/cli`         | Non-Vite app, CI, explicit generation command                                 |
| `@ic-reactor/codegen`     | Internal/shared generator pipeline; app users usually do not call it directly |

Generated canister directories usually contain declaration files, a managed
`index.generated.ts`, and a stable `index.ts` wrapper. Put custom app logic in
wrapper modules or factory files, not generated files.

### Codegen Consumer Flow

1. Configure `ic-reactor.json` (CLI) or `icReactor(...)` (Vite plugin).
2. Generate canister files.
3. Treat `index.generated.ts` as managed output.
4. Keep app-specific logic in `index.ts` or adjacent factory modules.
5. Re-run generation after `.did` changes.

Use CLI for explicit CI/manual generation; use Vite plugin for watch-mode local
development.

## Dynamic Candid

Use `@ic-reactor/candid` for explorers, dev tools, unknown canisters, metadata
forms, or Candid strings discovered at runtime. Use `@ic-reactor/parser` when
local `.did` parsing is needed; it ships WASM builds for browser and Node.js.

### Parser Import Path

`@ic-reactor/parser` has a single entrypoint:

```ts
import { didToJs, parseDid, validateIDL } from "@ic-reactor/parser"
```

There are no `/web`, `/nodejs`, or `/bundler` subpath exports — the package's
`exports` map declares only `"."` and `"./package.json"`. Conditional exports
pick the build: `browser`/`workerd`/default resolve to `dist/web`, and `node`
resolves to `dist/nodejs`. Do not deep-import `dist/`.

### Common Candid Patterns

Agents should account for these patterns in generated TypeScript:

- `Result` variants (`Ok`/`Err`, `ok`/`err`) are already unwrapped by the Reactor: `data` is the
  Ok payload, and an `Err` throws a `CanisterError` instead of ever reaching `data`. Do not write
  `"Ok" in data` guards — they can never be true. `callMethod()` unwraps too, so it is not an
  escape hatch; overriding `transformResult` on a Reactor subclass is the only way to receive the
  raw variant
- numeric Candid values (`nat`, `int`, etc.) are usually `bigint` in raw mode and strings in display mode
- `principal` values are `Principal` in raw mode and strings in display mode
- `opt T` often appears as tuples/options in raw actor shapes; UI flows should normalize these carefully
- large nested variants/records are common in ledger/governance canisters and benefit from reusable query/mutation factories

## Anti-Patterns to Avoid

- Calling React hooks in loaders/actions/services/tests
- Hard-coding query keys when `query.getQueryKey()` or `query.invalidate()` is available
- Editing `index.generated.ts` files directly
- Choosing raw `Reactor` for UI/form flows when display values were intended
- Duplicating codegen logic in app code instead of using CLI/Vite plugin configuration

## Example Routing by App Framework

| App stack | Recommended path |
| --------- | ---------------- |
| Vite + React | `@ic-reactor/vite-plugin` + generated declarations/hooks |
| Next.js (pages/app router) | CLI generation + factories; hooks in `"use client"` modules. On the server build the reactor per request (see SSR rule below) |
| TanStack Router | query/mutation factories with `.fetch()` for loaders and `.useQuery()` for components |
| Plain TS/node scripts | `@ic-reactor/core` + imperative APIs (`callMethod`, `fetchQuery`, `invalidateQueries`) |

### SSR rule

A reactor owns its `QueryClient`, and query keys are
`[canisterId, functionName, args]` with no caller principal. A module-scope
reactor on a server is therefore shared by every request, so a cached
caller-scoped result (`get_my_balance`, deposit address, `my_profile`) is served
to the next request. `AuthenticationManager` is worse: it holds mutable identity
state, and `createAuthHooks`' `useSyncExternalStore` server snapshot reads
whatever identity the shared manager happens to hold at render time.

Under SSR/RSC, construct the reactor, `ClientManager`, and
`AuthenticationManager` inside the request. A bare call in a module body is still
module scope, so the construction has to hang off something per-render — a
`useState` initializer inside a provider, which is what
`examples/nextjs/src/service/provider.tsx` does:

```tsx
import { createContext, useContext, useState } from "react"
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { ClientManager, AuthenticationManager } from "@ic-reactor/react"

function createReactorContext() {
  const queryClient = new QueryClient()
  const clientManager = new ClientManager({ queryClient })
  const authentication = new AuthenticationManager({ clientManager })
  const reactor = new Reactor<_SERVICE>({
    name: "backend",
    clientManager,
    canisterId,
    idlFactory,
  })
  return {
    queryClient,
    auth: createAuthHooks(authentication),
    todo: createActorHooks(reactor),
  }
}

const ReactorContext =
  createContext<ReturnType<typeof createReactorContext> | null>(null)

export function ICReactorProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  // The initializer runs once per mounted tree, and a server render is its own
  // tree, so each request gets its own managers and its own cache.
  const [value] = useState(createReactorContext)
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={value.queryClient}>
      <ReactorContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</ReactorContext.Provider>
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}
```

Module scope stays correct for client-only SPAs. Hooks are client-only; they
also bind to their reactor's own `QueryClient`, so `HydrationBoundary` prefetch
does not reach them unless the provider's client is that same instance.

## Generated File Boundaries

Avoid hand-editing:

- `dist/`
- `.dfx/`, `.icp/`, `.mops/`
- `target/`
- `.next/`, `.astro/`
- `*.tsbuildinfo`
- generated canister declarations
- generated hook files

When generated hooks or declarations are wrong, fix `packages/codegen/src/` and
verify the affected CLI/Vite consumer.

## Verification

| Change type           | Commands                                                                           |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Docs only             | `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm check:ai-context`, `pnpm docs:build`                    |
| AI context files      | `pnpm check:ai-context`                                                            |
| React hooks/factories | `pnpm --filter @ic-reactor/react test`                                             |
| Core runtime          | `pnpm --filter @ic-reactor/core test`                                              |
| React auth            | `pnpm --filter @ic-reactor/react test`                                             |
| Parser/candid         | `pnpm --filter @ic-reactor/parser build`, `pnpm --filter @ic-reactor/candid test`  |
| Codegen               | `pnpm --filter @ic-reactor/codegen test` plus affected CLI/Vite checks             |
| Broad package change  | `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm exec tsc -b`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test`                    |
| Package exports/build/module format | `pnpm verify:packages`                                               |
| Examples              | `pnpm typecheck:examples`, `pnpm build:examples`                                   |
| Docs site             | `pnpm docs:build`                                                                  |

Do not run package build and package test concurrently when parser/candid tests
depend on parser `dist`; parser builds remove and recreate `dist`.

Script notes:

- `pnpm format:check` globs `packages/**` only; root markdown, `docs/`,
  `examples/`, and `skill-packages/` are not covered by Prettier.
- `pnpm check:ai-context` is a CI gate asserting `llms.txt` package versions
  match each `package.json` and that every `packages/*/llms.txt` exists.
- `pnpm typecheck` runs each package's own `typecheck` script and covers tests
  as well as `src`. The root `tsconfig.json` is references-only, so
  `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` at the root type-checks nothing.
- `pnpm verify:packages` packs every publishable package, installs the tarballs
  outside the workspace, imports/requires each entry point in real Node, and
  runs `publint` + `attw`. It is the only check that sees what consumers get.
- `pnpm build:examples` is a CI gate alongside `pnpm typecheck:examples`. `tsc`
  never loads a bundler, so a broken Vite/Next config type-checks clean; both
  Next.js examples were unbuildable while the type-check job stayed green.
